title: Google Will Let You Switch Off Gemini's Watermark
hook: The little sparkle in the corner was the easiest way to tell a Google AI image from a real one. Now you can turn it off — so stop relying on visible marks.
key_points: The Verge reports a new 'Media watermark' toggle in Gemini and Google's video tool Flow.
Turning it off removes the sparkle badge from generated images, video, and music.
Visible badges were always the weakest signal — a crop or a toggle erases them.
Invisible watermarking, like Google's SynthID, is designed to survive edits instead.
Judge content by source and corroboration, not by whether a badge is present.
content_html: Google is adding a "Media watermark" setting to Gemini and Flow, its AI video generator. The Verge reports that switching it off removes the small sparkle badge Google has been stamping into the corner of AI-generated images, videos, and music.
extra_html: If you had been using that sparkle as your tell, this is a good moment to retire the habit. Visible badges are convenience labels, not security features — they survive only until someone crops the image or, now, flips a switch. The more durable approach is invisible watermarking such as Google's SynthID, which is meant to persist through edits and be checked by a tool rather than an eye. For everyday judgment, though, neither replaces the boring method that works: ask where a striking image came from, and see whether anyone credible reports the same thing independently.

related.title: Spotting AI-Made Content
related.hook: There are real tells for AI text and images — but they're fading fast, and 'AI detector' tools are unreliable. The durable skill is judging the source, not squinting at the pixels.

related.title: Meta Built Its Own AI Watermark Instead of Using the Shared One
related.hook: Meta's new 'Content Seal' stamps an invisible mark on its AI images so they can be traced. The catch: Google already had a tool for that — and one shared standard works better than many.

related.title: The Biggest AI Music Maker Wants to Label Its Own Songs
related.hook: Suno is adding watermarking and download rules to stem the flood of AI tracks clogging streaming services — a rare case of a generator volunteering to mark its output.

flashcards.prompt: What changed with Google's new 'Media watermark' setting?

choices.text: Users can turn off the visible sparkle badge on Gemini and Flow output
Google now adds a watermark to every image on the web
Watermarks became legally required in the EU

flashcards.explanation_html: The toggle removes the visible corner badge from images, video, and music generated in Gemini and Flow.

flashcards.prompt: Why was a visible watermark never a reliable way to spot AI content?
flashcards.back_html: It can be cropped, edited out, or — as here — simply switched off. Absence of a badge has never been evidence that something is real.

flashcards.prompt: What should you use instead of a badge to judge a suspicious image?
flashcards.back_html: Where it came from and whether anyone else independently reports the same thing. Provenance and corroboration outlast any mark on the pixels.
